name: Montenegro
summary_text: Montenegro is workable for trans visitors — the Western Balkans' most advanced legal framework. It has a same-sex partnership law (2020), anti-discrimination law covering gender identity, and SOGI-inclusive hate-crime provisions; Podgorica Pride proceeds annually. Counterweights documented by ILGA-Europe: anti-LGBT and misogynistic hate speech in political rhetoric is a serious issue, and misdemeanour charges are overused in place of proper hate-crime prosecution (European Commission). There is no legal gender recognition law (administrative practice is inconsistent). For a visitor: no legal exposure, functioning institutions, small tolerant coastal tourist scene; standard caution in the north.

sources.claim_summary: ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2024 (covering 2023) chapter on Montenegro: anti-LGBT and misogynistic hate speech and political rhetoric continued; a psychologist wearing non-gender-conforming clothes on TV was targeted by hate comments, threats and several physical attacks (police response monitored); a groundbreaking study found only 28.1% of companies' anti-discrimination policies explicitly mention sexual orientation; a new Action Plan for the 2019-2023 LGBTI Strategy was adopted with €45,000; over 222 online hate-speech incidents reported.

sources.title: A History of LGBT Criminalisation | Human Dignity Trust
sources.claim_summary: Human Dignity Trust: 'A History of LGBT Criminalisation' - overview of criminalising jurisdictions and strategic litigation (Montenegro context: decriminalised in 1977 under Yugoslavia).

sources.title: Gay Life in Montenegro
sources.claim_summary: GlobalGayz 'Gay Life in Montenegro: Past and Present' (March 2012): decriminalised in 1977; both male and female same-sex activity legal; equal age of consent at 14; same-sex couples lack the legal rights of married couples - historical and cultural context from Ottoman rule to independence.

sources.title: Montenegro’s gay pride march sparks violence | News | Al Jazeera
sources.claim_summary: Al Jazeera (Oct 2013): Montenegro's first Podgorica Pride - ~2,000 police guarded ~150 marchers; tear gas used against rock-throwing opponents; organiser Danijel Kalezic: 'From this day we are no longer invisible'; the march seen as a test of Montenegro's EU human-rights commitments.

sources.title: Montenegro politicians block law recognising same-sex unions | PinkNews
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (Aug 2019): Montenegro's politicians blocked the same-sex partnership law (July 31) despite backing from the governing DPS; conservative Democratic Front deputy Jovan Vucurovic: 'After this law a law on adoption of children by LGBT population will follow'; the Equal Rights Association said LGBT+ people are 'forced to live in hiding'.

sources.title: LGBT couples in Montenegro will be allowed to marry but not to be parents - CdM
sources.claim_summary: CDM/Dan (Dec 2018): the Government defined the Draft Law on Same-Sex Partnership - granting same-sex couples the same rights as heterosexuals except parenting: no fostering, no adoption; law to enter into force one year after parliamentary adoption.
